title: How to Find Deals on Secondhand Furniture
summary: 5 tips for finding the best secondhand furniture at the best price. You can score amazing pieces from top brands using search and shopping tools.
body_markdown:
Good fur­ni­ture costs more than most peo­ple want to spend. A sol­id hard­wood dress­er typ­i­cal­ly starts at $1000 new. The same piece, two years old with a cou­ple of scuffs on the back, goes for $250 if you know where to look.


Here is exact­ly how to find those pieces.


### **1. Stop Scrolling Facebook Marketplace Randomly**


Most peo­ple open the app, type “couch,” scroll for 20 min­utes, and close it. That is not how you find deals.


Set up saved search­es and set alerts. Search for the spe­cif­ic piece you want, the mate­r­i­al, and a rough era (“mid-cen­tu­ry,” “sol­id oak,” “boucle”). Then let the plat­form bring list­ings to you instead of hunt­ing man­u­al­ly. The best pieces sell with­in hours of post­ing, so first-mover advan­tage mat­ters more than search volume.


How­ev­er, wait­ing for local inven­to­ry can take time. Don’t expect an imme­di­ate score.


### **2. Use a Curated Resale Platform for Quality Pieces**


Gen­er­al mar­ket­places like Craigslist and Face­book Mar­ket­place are fine for basic items, but the list­ing qual­i­ty, pho­tos, and sell­er account­abil­i­ty vary wild­ly. If you want design­er or high-end sec­ond­hand fur­ni­ture with­out the risk of dri­ving 45 min­utes to look at some­thing that turns out to be par­ti­cle board, use a plat­form built for *vet­ted* resale.


[Apt­De­co](https://www.aptdeco.com/) lists pre-owned fur­ni­ture from brands like West Elm, Restora­tion Hard­ware, Crate & Bar­rel, and Design With­in Reach at 40% — 70% below retail. The pieces are pho­tographed in detail, dimen­sions are con­firmed, and the plat­form han­dles white-glove pick­up and deliv­ery, so you are not rent­ing a van.


If you have a spe­cif­ic piece in mind, search Apt­De­co by brand or style first. The inven­to­ry turns over quick­ly, so check back reg­u­lar­ly or set up alerts for your pre­ferred categories.


### **3. Time Your Search to Match When Sellers List**


Sec­ond­hand fur­ni­ture list­ings clus­ter around pre­dictable life events:


- End of month: Leas­es end, peo­ple move, and any­thing that won’t fit in a U‑Haul gets list­ed fast.
- **Late sum­mer:** Col­lege stu­dents and recent grad­u­ates fur­nish new apart­ments in August and Sep­tem­ber. The ones who over­bought list their extras short­ly after.
- **Spring:** Post-tax-refund ren­o­va­tions push old­er pieces out.
- **After the hol­i­days:** Gift­ed fur­ni­ture that does­n’t work in a space gets resold in January.


Search more active­ly dur­ing these win­dows. You will find more list­ings and more moti­vat­ed sellers.


### **4. Know What You Are Actually Looking At**


A low price means noth­ing if the piece needs $300 in repairs. Before you com­mit, check for:


- Sol­id wood vs. venee **r.** Look over the piece close­ly or exam­ine pho­tos. Veneer chips and swells. Sol­id wood refin­ish­es cleanly.
- **Pay atten­tion to the details.** Sit on chairs and sofas, try out draw­ers. Not in per­son? Read any “con­di­tion” notes close­ly to make sure you under­stand any knicks or scratch­es in advance.
- **Ask ques­tions.** Don’t feel like you have a good under­stand­ing of the con­di­tion of the item? Ask the sell­er for more details.


A pre-loved piece with cos­met­ic wear, a scratch on the top, or out­dat­ed hard­ware is absolute­ly worth buy­ing. A piece with struc­tur­al prob­lems is usu­al­ly not.


### **5. Think in Total Cost, Not Sticker Price**


A free couch you find on the curb costs $80 in rent­ed truck time, $40 in gas, and four hours of a Sat­ur­day if you need help mov­ing it. A $350 couch on Apt­De­co that includes white-glove deliv­ery to your door costs less, once you account for everything.


Cal­cu­late deliv­ery fees, any clean­ing or repairs the piece needs, and the time cost of pick­up before decid­ing a low­er stick­er price is actu­al­ly the bet­ter deal.


### **Where to Start Today**


If you have a spe­cif­ic piece in mind, check[Apt­De­co](https://www.aptdeco.com/) first for vet­ted sec­ond­hand inven­to­ry with han­dled logis­tics. For a broad­er search, set up saved search alerts on Face­book Mar­ket­place and Craigslist for your exact item, mate­r­i­al, and style. Then be patient. The right piece at the right price shows up. The buy­ers who find it are the ones who have already set up their alerts and know what they are will­ing to pay.
